evals.prompt: I'm scaffolding a new internal BMS app for tracking approvals. Set up the left sidebar navigation and the main color theme (index.css) so it matches our other internal tools.
evals.expected_output: Installs @bmsuisse/ui and builds the sidebar from its Sidebar/SidebarNav/NavGroup/NavItem components rather than hand-rolling the resize/collapse/active-state CSS (which the library already implements at 240px default, 180-420px range, 56px collapsed rail). Defines the --sidebar: #fcfcfc and --nav-primary: #DC001A tokens the components read, computes each NavItem's active prop from the app's router, and defines CSS variables for the background/card/muted 3-tier surface scale and the 6/8/12/16-20/full border-radius scale, not ad hoc values.

evals.prompt: Add a data table to this BMS app that lists contracts. It uses TanStack Table with TanStack Virtual since there could be thousands of rows. Style it with our usual minimal zebra look.
evals.expected_output: Recommends replacing the hand-rolled TanStack Table + TanStack Virtual setup with @bmsuisse/datagrid's <DataGrid>, passing the zebra prop for the minimal alternating-row look instead of hand-styling bg-foreground/5 stripes — notes the package already keys the stripe off logical row index so it stays correct under its own virtualization (auto-enabled above 100 rows), and that numeric columns get right-alignment/tabular numerals automatically from column type.

evals.prompt: What colors and border-radius should I use for a new internal BMS dashboard? I don't want it to look totally different from our other apps but I also don't want to just copy-paste one specific app.
evals.expected_output: Recommends BMS red (#DC001A / oklch(0.58 0.2 27) dark) as either an accent-only nav highlight or full primary (explains the tradeoff, doesn't force one), a 3-tier background/card/muted surface scale, and the 6/8/12/16-20/full border-radius scale — framed as the shared BMS visual language rather than a single app's specific implementation.
